description:
The Advance Authorisation (AA) scheme is a significant initiative under the Foreign Trade Policy of India.

It was introduced in 2009 to promote exports by providing duty-free import of inputs.

The scheme aims to enhance the competitiveness of Indian exporters in the global market.

The primary objective of the Advance Authorisation scheme is to allow exporters to import inputs without paying customs duties.

This is intended to reduce the overall cost of production for exporters.

The scheme is particularly beneficial for the manufacturing sector.

It allows for the import of raw materials that are used in the production of goods meant for export.

The Advance Authorisation can be issued for both physical exports and deemed exports.

The scheme covers a wide range of products including textiles, leather, chemicals, and engineering goods.

Under this scheme, exporters can import inputs up to a specific value.

The value is determined based on the value addition required in the export product.

Typically, the value addition requirement is set at 15%.

This means that the exporter must add at least 15% value to the imported inputs before exporting the final product.

The Advance Authorisation is valid for a period of 12 months from the date of issue.

This allows exporters sufficient time to utilize the imported inputs.

The scheme also allows for the transfer of authorisation.

This means that the authorisation can be transferred to another manufacturer or exporter.

The eligibility criteria for the Advance Authorisation scheme are specific.

Any manufacturer-exporter or merchant-exporter can apply for this scheme.

The applicant must be registered with the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT).

The applicant must also have a valid Importer Exporter Code (IEC).

There are no specific age limits for applicants under this scheme.

However, the applicant must demonstrate a track record of export performance.

This is generally assessed based on the export turnover in the previous financial year.

The application process for the Advance Authorisation is straightforward.

Applicants must submit an application to the DGFT.

The application must include details of the export product and the inputs required.

The applicant must also provide a self-declaration regarding the value addition.

Required documents include the IEC certificate, a copy of the export order, and a bank certificate.

The bank certificate must confirm the availability of funds for the import of inputs.

Once the application is submitted, it is processed by the DGFT.

The processing time for the application is typically around 15 working days.

Upon approval, the Advance Authorisation is issued to the applicant.

The authorisation specifies the quantity and value of inputs that can be imported.

The disbursement of benefits under the scheme occurs at the time of import.

Exporters can claim the duty exemption at the time of customs clearance.

The Advance Authorisation scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

The Directorate General of Foreign Trade is the primary authority overseeing the scheme.

Contact details for the DGFT can be found on their official website.

The scheme is reviewed periodically to ensure its effectiveness.

The government has made several amendments to the scheme over the years.

These amendments aim to simplify the process and expand the scope of the scheme.

For instance, in 2015, the government introduced the concept of 'zero-duty' Advance Authorisation.

This allows for the import of inputs without any customs duty.

The scheme has contributed significantly to India's export growth.

According to the Ministry of Commerce, exports from India reached USD 400 billion in the financial year 2021-2022.

The Advance Authorisation scheme plays a crucial role in this achievement.

The scheme has also been instrumental in promoting Make in India.

It encourages domestic manufacturing by providing duty-free access to essential inputs.

The scheme is particularly beneficial for small and medium enterprises.

These enterprises often face challenges in accessing capital for imports.

By reducing the cost of inputs, the scheme helps improve their competitiveness.

The government has also introduced online facilities for applying under the scheme.

This has streamlined the application process and reduced processing times.

Exporters can now apply for Advance Authorisation through the DGFT's online portal.

The online system allows for real-time tracking of applications.

This transparency helps in reducing delays and improving efficiency.

The scheme is part of a broader strategy to enhance India's export capabilities.

It aligns with the government's vision of increasing the contribution of exports to GDP.

The government aims to increase the share of exports in GDP to 25% by 2025.

The Advance Authorisation scheme is a vital tool in achieving this goal.

It supports various sectors including textiles, pharmaceuticals, and engineering.

The scheme has also been aligned with the Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime.

Exporters can claim refunds on input tax credits under the GST.

This further enhances the financial viability of exporting under the Advance Authorisation scheme.

In conclusion, the Advance Authorisation scheme is a comprehensive initiative.

It provides significant benefits to exporters by allowing duty-free imports of inputs.

The scheme has specific eligibility criteria and a straightforward application process.

It is implemented by the DGFT under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

The scheme has evolved over the years to meet the changing needs of exporters.

It plays a crucial role in enhancing India's export competitiveness on the global stage.
